# Per-project idle-workbench report in the RHOAI web console

## Description

This epic delivers a per-project idle-workbench report in the RHOAI web console, giving cluster administrators visibility into workbenches that are sitting idle. For each workbench in a project, the report shows the last activity timestamp, the owner, and the reserved resources (volumes and compute reservations), so admins can identify reclaimable capacity with confidence. The report is sourced from the notebook controller's existing activity tracking — no notebook controller code changes are required. The report is surfaced under a shared per-project idle-resource reporting area of the web console, alongside the stale pipeline-run report, so administrators find both idle-resource views in one place. The report also supports CSV export so administrators can take the data offline for planning.

## Scope

- New per-project report view in the web console listing workbenches with:
  - Last activity timestamp (sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking)
  - Workbench owner
  - Reserved resources (volumes and reservations held by the workbench)
- Console-side data sourcing from the notebook controller's existing last-activity tracking (API-surface discovery for how the console consumes this data is part of this epic's implementation; no changes to the notebook controller itself)
- Report is surfaced in the shared per-project idle-resource reporting area of the console navigation, alongside the stale pipeline-run report (both views reachable from one reporting entry point)
- CSV export of the idle-workbench report, covering the rows and columns displayed in the report (administrators can export the report for offline use). CSV export is a separable P2 increment: the export action is additive to the report page and can be delivered after the report view itself — including shipping initially disabled behind a feature flag — without redoing the report's data sourcing, so deferring the export does not reopen the shipped report surface
- Report is read-only: reclamation decisions and actions remain manual and out of scope

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches, when an administrator opens the idle-workbench report for that project, then the report lists each workbench with its last activity timestamp, owner, and reserved resources.
- Given workbenches with differing activity histories, when the report is viewed, then idle workbenches are distinguishable from recently used ones based on the notebook controller's tracked activity.
- The report's last-activity data matches the notebook controller's tracked activity for the corresponding workbenches (validation that the notebook controller's activity tracking keeps working unchanged as the data source — the notebook controller is a passive component in this strategy).
- No code changes are made to the notebook controller; the report consumes its existing activity tracking.
- Given the idle-workbench report, when an administrator exports it as CSV, then a CSV file is produced containing the report's rows (workbench, last activity, owner, reserved resources).
- Given a project with 200 or more workbenches, when an administrator opens the idle-workbench report, then the report view renders within 5 seconds (thresholds are a planning assumption to confirm with the dashboard team — the strategy defines no performance requirements).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)**: The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking. — Primary coverage.
- **HLR-3 (P2)**: Administrators can export either report as CSV. — Covers CSV export for the idle-workbench report. Bundled here (rather than a separate epic) because the export action lives on the same report UI surface and operates on the same report data; it is a separable increment within this epic (can ship later or behind a feature flag) so the P2 export can be deferred without reopening the shipped report.

# Stale pipeline-run report in the RHOAI web console

## Description

This epic delivers a per-project stale pipeline-run report in the RHOAI web console, showing completed pipeline runs older than a configurable age that still retain artifacts. This lets cluster administrators find old runs whose accumulated artifacts consume storage. The report is sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines' existing run completion metadata — no Kubeflow Pipelines code changes are required. The report is surfaced under a shared per-project idle-resource reporting area of the web console, alongside the idle-workbench report, so administrators find both idle-resource views in one place. The report also supports CSV export.

## Scope

- New per-project report view in the web console listing completed pipeline runs that:
  - Completed earlier than a configurable age threshold
  - Retain artifacts (e.g., stored run artifacts/output)
- Console-side data sourcing from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata (run completion timestamps and artifact retention state); no changes to Kubeflow Pipelines itself
- Administrator-configurable age threshold for what counts as "stale" (the configuration mechanism is an implementation decision for the console team)
- Report is surfaced in the shared per-project idle-resource reporting area of the console navigation, alongside the idle-workbench report (both views reachable from one reporting entry point)
- CSV export of the stale pipeline-run report, covering the rows and columns displayed in the report. CSV export is a separable P2 increment: the export action is additive to the report page and can be delivered after the report view itself — including shipping initially disabled behind a feature flag — without redoing the report's data sourcing, so deferring the export does not reopen the shipped report surface
- Report is read-only: artifact cleanup/reclamation remains manual and out of scope

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project with completed pipeline runs of varying ages, when an administrator opens the stale pipeline-run report, then the report lists completed runs older than the configured age that retain artifacts.
- Given the report, when an administrator changes the stale age threshold, then the report reflects the new threshold without requiring a console restart or redeployment.
- The report's run data (completion times, artifact retention) matches Kubeflow Pipelines' run metadata for the corresponding runs (validation that Kubeflow Pipelines keeps working unchanged as the data source — it is a passive component in this strategy).
- No code changes are made to Kubeflow Pipelines; the report consumes its existing run metadata.
- Given the stale pipeline-run report, when an administrator exports it as CSV, then a CSV file is produced containing the report's rows.
- Given a project with 1,000 or more completed pipeline runs, when an administrator opens the stale pipeline-run report, then the report view renders within 5 seconds (thresholds are a planning assumption to confirm with the dashboard team — the strategy defines no performance requirements).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P1)**: The web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. — Primary coverage.
- **HLR-3 (P2)**: Administrators can export either report as CSV. — Covers CSV export for the stale pipeline-run report. Bundled here (rather than a separate epic) because the export action lives on the same report UI surface and operates on the same report data; it is a separable increment within this epic (can ship later or behind a feature flag) so the P2 export can be deferred without reopening the shipped report.

# Documentation for idle resource reports and safe reclamation steps

## Description

This epic delivers Red Hat documentation explaining the two new console reports — the per-project idle-workbench report and the stale pipeline-run report — and the safe manual steps administrators can take to reclaim capacity based on them. It gives administrators the context to interpret each report correctly and to act on it without accidentally deleting resources that are still needed.

## Scope

- New documentation topics covering:
  - The idle-workbench report: what it shows (last activity, owner, reserved resources), where to find it, and how to interpret the activity data
  - The stale pipeline-run report: what it shows (completed runs older than the configurable age with retained artifacts), where to find it, and how to configure the age threshold
  - CSV export of either report
  - Safe reclamation steps: how administrators can manually reclaim idle workbench resources and stale pipeline-run artifacts based on the reports, including cautions about resources that may still be needed
- Documentation follows the Red Hat docs content process and tooling
- Out of scope (per strategy): documentation of automated reclamation or cost/chargeback — these capabilities do not exist

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the shipped reports, when a reader consults the documentation, then both reports are explained: purpose, location in the web console, columns/data shown, and how to export as CSV.
- The documentation includes safe reclamation guidance for both idle workbenches and stale pipeline-run artifacts, with appropriate cautions.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented reports (content verified by the implementing team to match actual report behavior and data semantics).
- The documentation contains no description of automated reclamation or chargeback features (they are out of scope for the strategy).
- Documentation accurately reflects the notebook controller activity tracking and Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata semantics the reports are sourced from.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)**: Documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps. — Full coverage.
